section_summary: The section opens with the end of a Japanese statistical publication covering securities, prices, bonds and capital. A 1946 occupation report then describes the closure and liquidation of wartime financial institutions, with institutional profiles, accounts and control charts. The later records concern Bank of Taiwan depositors, Japanese and foreign banking services, and proposals to restore remittances between the United States and Japan.

subfiles.title: Japanese financial and price statistics, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Concluding statistical tables report Japanese securities trading, prices, debt issues and capital through 1946.
subfiles.summary: Tables cover Tokyo stock trading and security values, wholesale and retail prices, government and short term securities, bonds, planned capital and paid-up capital. The final page gives publication and printing details.

subfiles.title: Report of Activities of Liquidation Branch, Finance Division, ESS
subfiles.about: Reports the first year of occupation work closing and liquidating colonial and wartime financial institutions.
subfiles.summary: The report explains the seizure, examination, liquidation and claims phases, including the roles of the Bank of Japan and Committee of Conservators. It estimates closed institutions' book assets above ¥175 billion and describes their extensive loans and stock holdings. It also sets asset-sale approvals, public auction procedures, depositor payments and the unresolved questions of external claims and final accounting.

subfiles.title: Chronological Summary of Policy Directives Issued the Imperial Japanese Government
subfiles.about: Lists occupation directives on closure, conservatorship and liquidation.
subfiles.summary: Chronology of SCAP directives from September 1945 to October 1946.

subfiles.title: Institutions Closed and Responsible Japanese Liquidating Agents
subfiles.about: Identifies closed institutions, closure dates and assigned liquidating agents.
subfiles.summary: Lists 46 institutions and defines conservation, liquidation and agent abbreviations.

subfiles.title: Basic Profiles of Closed Institutions
subfiles.about: Profiles the capital, ownership, headquarters and operations of closed banks and companies.
subfiles.summary: The profiles describe banks, development companies, industrial firms, railways and wartime finance bodies across Japan and its former occupied territories. Each entry summarizes capitalization, principal interests, head office, area of operation and Japanese office functions. The appendix shows the institutions' strong links to government-directed expansion, military finance and industrial control.

subfiles.title: Relations of Liquidation Branch with Japanese Government and Liquidating Components
subfiles.about: Charts supervision, liaison and funds flow among occupation and Japanese liquidation bodies.
subfiles.summary: Shows agency relationships and liquidation proceeds flow.

subfiles.title: Closed Institutions Liquidation Report, Schedule I
subfiles.about: Summarizes assets, liquidation proceeds and costs by agent.
subfiles.summary: Reports aggregate book assets of about ¥175.6 billion and assets liquidated of about ¥1.4 billion.

subfiles.title: Closed Institutions Liquidation Report, Schedule II
subfiles.about: Itemizes domestic assets, proceeds and liquidation costs by closed institution.
subfiles.summary: This three-page schedule compares book values at closure and at 30 September 1946 for individual institutions. It gives values liquidated, proceeds and costs, with totals for the Bank of Japan, Hypothec Bank and Committee of Conservators.

subfiles.title: Closed Institutions Liquidation Report, Schedule III
subfiles.about: Classifies liquidated assets and proceeds by asset type.
subfiles.summary: Lists bonds, stocks, loans, property and other assets.

subfiles.title: Departmental Organization of Japanese Liquidating Agents
subfiles.about: Charts Japanese liquidating agents' departments and funds flow.
subfiles.summary: Shows accounts, disposal, collections, creditors and claims functions.

subfiles.title: Audit Control—Liquidation Activities
subfiles.about: Diagrams financial reporting and audit controls for liquidation.
subfiles.summary: Connects receipts, expenses, claims, budgets and monthly accounts.

subfiles.title: Flow Chart on Disposal of Assets
subfiles.about: Shows disposal proceeds and approval thresholds for asset sales.
subfiles.summary: Sets approval levels from Japanese agents to the Chief of ESS.

subfiles.title: CCCI Distribution of General Expenses
subfiles.from: Committee of Conservators for Closed Institutions
subfiles.about: Explains how shared liquidation expenses are allocated.
subfiles.summary: Direct costs go to institutions; general costs follow staff hours.

subfiles.title: General Expenses of Committee of Conservators and Allocation
subfiles.from: Committee of Conservators for Closed Institutions
subfiles.about: Requests transfers allocating September expenses among closed institutions.
subfiles.summary: The committee asks the Bank of Japan to charge closed institutions and credit its overhead account. An attached schedule distributes ¥10,184.90 in general expenses and ¥48,076.72 in institution-specific payments.

subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Notice
subfiles.about: Designates a white telegram copy as the file record copy.
subfiles.summary: The yellow action copy had not been returned.

subfiles.title: Routing Slip
subfiles.about: Routes a document for action or information.
subfiles.summary: Names possible recipients and handling choices.

subfiles.title: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs Action Cable Form
subfiles.from: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Provides fields for assigning and tracking cable action.
subfiles.summary: Largely blank action and comments form.

subfiles.title: Bank of Taiwan Depositors
subfiles.about: Urges immediate payment of most Bank of Taiwan depositors.
subfiles.summary: Reports approximately 21,400 depositors and sufficient cash to pay most claims, while seeking clarification on seven large balances.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal of Proposed State Cable on Banking Services
subfiles.to: Assistant Secretary of State for Occupied Areas
subfiles.about: Recommends withdrawing a redundant draft cable to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Chard says SCAP had already received and concurred in the relevant SWNCC proposal.

subfiles.title: Inquiry About Japanese Banks and Yasuda Bank
subfiles.to: Commercial Intelligence Division, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Asks about Japanese banks' operating conditions, foreign exchange prospects and Yasuda Bank.
subfiles.summary: Irving Trust cites a Yasuda Bank letter proposing eventual renewed relations and requests confidential guidance.

subfiles.title: Referral of Irving Trust Inquiry
subfiles.from: Charles K. Moser, Department of Commerce
subfiles.to: Edwin M. Martin, Department of State
subfiles.about: Refers Irving Trust's Japanese banking questions to State.
subfiles.summary: The Far Eastern Division forwards the June 25 letter following a telephone discussion.

subfiles.title: Department of State Charge Slip
subfiles.about: Records the charge-out of a document concerning Irving Trust.
subfiles.summary: The handwritten document description is largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Suggestions on SWNCC 226/8
subfiles.about: Proposes procedural revisions to a banking facilities policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Burton questions its phrasing, linkage to another pending paper and proposed filing with the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.title: Amendments to SWNCC 226/8
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, State Department member, SWNCC
subfiles.about: Seeks circulation of amended appendices on foreign trade banking in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum argues that SCAP already has authority to license foreign bank branches and asks that the U.S. Government express approval rather than issue an instruction.

subfiles.title: Proposed Cable to SCAP on Commercial and Foreign Trade Banking Facilities
subfiles.about: Proposes licensing foreign bank branches to support Japanese foreign trade.
subfiles.summary: The amended cable recognizes SCAP's existing authority to license qualified foreign banks for export-import and related services. It proposes first-come licensing subject to facilities and other constraints, excludes enemy and former enemy banks, and includes a draft public announcement.

subfiles.title: Amended Recommendations for SWNCC 226/8
subfiles.about: Revises procedural recommendations for transmitting the proposed banking cable and issuing a press release.
subfiles.summary: Marked changes call for sending the cable to SCAP and releasing the announcement after SCAP advises on timing, while removing a link to a pending FEC paper.

subfiles.title: Earlier Draft of Amendment Memorandum and Press Release
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, State Department member, SWNCC
subfiles.about: Shows edited language on SCAP authority and the foreign-bank press release.
subfiles.summary: A heavily marked memorandum requests replacement appendices to SWNCC 226/8. Its final page continues draft press-release language on licensing foreign bank branches and the shortage of physical facilities.

subfiles.title: Reestablishment of Remittance Facilities Through Banking Channels
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, State Department member, SWNCC
subfiles.about: Submits a State member statement on proposed remittance facilities.
subfiles.summary: Requests circulation of the attached statement for committee consideration.

subfiles.title: Statement by the State Member on Remittance Proceeds
subfiles.about: Opposes diverting commercial remittance proceeds to the Army troop-pay account.
subfiles.summary: The statement distinguishes civilian remittances from expenditures under a May 1947 understanding on recovery of dollars for Army-held yen. It argues that remittance proceeds are held in trust for Japan's economy and ordinarily enter the trade account. It warns that diverting them to troop pay would change that treatment and invite criticism, and recommends approving SWNCC 226/9 without the War member's amendments.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Approved SWNCC 226/9
subfiles.to: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Encloses the approved paper on commercial remittances between the United States and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes committee approval on October 23 and that the referenced SWNCC 226/4 is unavailable.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Approved SWNCC 226/6
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Coordinating Committee chairman
subfiles.about: Forwards the approved foreign trade banking paper and describes implementation steps.
subfiles.summary: Reports approval at the October 3 meeting and requests copies of State's implementing action.

subfiles.title: Decision Amending SWNCC 226/6
subfiles.about: Directs page replacements following approval of revised banking proposals.
subfiles.summary: Calls for replacing specified pages, adding page 59a and ending consideration of SWNCC 226/7.

subfiles.title: Establishment of Commercial and Foreign Trade Banking Facilities in Japan
subfiles.about: Introduces a State member proposal for priority consideration.
subfiles.summary: The paper's cover note circulates its enclosure to the committee.
